luca-a-roma-34:s08: Then the door opened. Marco arrived with bread from a nearby shop.
luca-a-roma-34:s09: There was a call. It was a short time. Now I am here.
luca-a-roma-34:s11: Yes. But the bread is here, and I am too. What do I do?
luca-a-roma-34:s12: Luca smiled a little. The Saturday-morning problem was not closed, but it was different.
luca-a-roma-34:s13: Sofia arrived after, with new messages on the phone.
luca-a-roma-34:s14: Some people say yes. Some people say maybe. I don’t know yet.
luca-a-roma-34:s15: Then we prepare anyway. If they come, we are ready.
luca-a-roma-34:s16: The owner came out of the kitchen for a moment and looked at the young people and the tables.
luca-a-roma-34:s17: All right. I stay in the kitchen. If needed, I call.
luca-a-roma-34:s18: They put out the plates, the water, and the coffee. Luca washed the tables twice.
luca-a-roma-34:s19: Giulia chose a place for the music, not too loud, near the window.
luca-a-roma-34:s20: What do you say? This way people can talk.
luca-a-roma-34:s21: It seems right to me. We don’t want music that closes off the voices.
luca-a-roma-34:s22: Marco prepared the bread and put the plates near the kitchen.
luca-a-roma-34:s23: Sofia wrote a small sign on the door: “Today, celebration. Come.”
luca-a-roma-34:s24: I stay near the messages. If someone asks the time, I answer.
luca-a-roma-34:s25: I stay at the door. When people arrive, I say good morning.
luca-a-roma-34:s26: I serve. If bread is needed, I call Marco.
luca-a-roma-34:s27: All right. If nobody comes, at least we did the work.
luca-a-roma-34:s28: Before the celebration, the room was ready. There was still little voice.
luca-a-roma-34:s29: Luca looked at his friends and thought of the week’s plan.
luca-a-roma-34:s30: The tables, the coffee, and the bread were ready. Now they had to wait.
luca-a-roma-34:s31: If few people come, it doesn’t matter. We did something.
luca-a-roma-34:s32: Yes. But I want people here. For Giulia, for the owner, for us.
luca-a-roma-34:s33: Let’s wait. In the afternoon we see if the plan works.
luca-a-roma-34:s34: Sofia put the phone on the table and looked at the closed door.
luca-a-roma-34:s35: On the neighborhood street there were already voices, but in the room there was still nobody.
luca-a-roma-34:s36: Marco looked at the bread another time.
luca-a-roma-34:s37: Luca opened the door a little and waited.
luca-a-roma-34:s38: We did our work. Now we wait for the people.
luca-a-roma-34:s39: Yes. Today we cannot do more.
luca-a-roma-34:s40: It was still morning. The celebration had not started yet.
luca-a-roma-34:s41: But for the first time on Saturday, Marco was there with them, ready to work.
luca-a-roma-34:s42: When the owner went back to the kitchen, the room was ready and empty.
luca-a-roma-34:s43: Luca felt the fear, but he was also a little glad.
luca-a-roma-34:s44: The café was ready. The people, not yet.
luca-a-roma-34:s45: Now the work remains. Then we see who comes in.
luca-a-roma-35:s01: In the early afternoon the room was still almost empty.
luca-a-roma-35:s02: Luca stood at the door and said good morning to people who passed, but few came in.
luca-a-roma-35:s04: Wait. It is early. Neighborhood people eat and then go out.
luca-a-roma-35:s05: Giulia brought coffee to an empty table, only to do something.
luca-a-roma-35:s06: The owner watched from the kitchen, without smiling.
luca-a-roma-35:s07: Marco looked at the bread and did not talk much.
luca-a-roma-35:s08: Then Nonna Rosa arrived, with an old friend and with a strong voice.
luca-a-roma-35:s09: So, we are here. Where is the coffee? And the bread?
luca-a-roma-35:s10: Marco smiled and brought bread and water. The room was no longer completely empty.
luca-a-roma-35:s11: After Nonna Rosa three people from the neighborhood arrived, then a family. Some people were there because Sofia had written to them.
luca-a-roma-35:s13: Luca kept standing at the door, a little less tired.
luca-a-roma-35:s14: A woman asked about the hours. Sofia answered calmly.
luca-a-roma-35:s15: In an hour the room was almost full. There was music, voices, and there was coffee.
luca-a-roma-35:s16: Sofia was talking with people. Giulia was serving. Marco was helping with the plates, and two people were still waiting.
luca-a-roma-35:s17: The owner came out of the kitchen and looked at the full tables, a little surprised.
luca-a-roma-35:s18: So many people. I had not seen this in a long time.
luca-a-roma-35:s19: They are neighborhood people. They wanted a reason to come.
luca-a-roma-35:s20: A woman said she liked the coffee, and that she would come back the next week.
luca-a-roma-35:s21: Luca brought water to a table and listened to people talk about Rome and work.
luca-a-roma-35:s22: He did not understand all the words, but he understood the important thing: the room was alive.
luca-a-roma-35:s23: You are good at the door. People see you and come in.
luca-a-roma-35:s24: Thanks. Today I work here with you, not alone.
luca-a-roma-35:s25: The owner served two coffees and looked at the room again.
luca-a-roma-35:s26: It works, at least today. I don’t know about Monday.
luca-a-roma-35:s27: Today counts. The people are here now.
luca-a-roma-35:s28: Some customers asked if there was a celebration the next week too.
luca-a-roma-35:s29: Not every Saturday. But the café is open. You can come back.
luca-a-roma-35:s30: Marco brought bread to Nonna Rosa and listened to the voices near the tables.
luca-a-roma-35:s31: When a family came in late, Luca found a place near the window.
luca-a-roma-35:s32: The music stayed not too loud. People stayed to talk.
luca-a-roma-35:s33: Giulia looked at Luca and made a small sign: it was going well.
luca-a-roma-35:s34: The owner did not make big speeches. He only worked and watched.
luca-a-roma-35:s36: But after weeks of empty tables, today there were customers and friends together.
luca-a-roma-35:s37: Nonna Rosa called Luca and told him to stay near the door.
luca-a-roma-35:s38: People come in if they see someone. You stay there.
luca-a-roma-35:s40: Sofia put the phone on the table. Now the phone was no longer needed.
luca-a-roma-35:s41: The small celebration was working, at least for these hours.
luca-a-roma-35:s42: Luca felt less fear, but he did not say that the problem was finished.
luca-a-roma-35:s43: The owner was seeing customers. That was more important than words.
luca-a-roma-35:s44: Toward evening some people left, and some people stayed longer.
luca-a-roma-35:s45: Now Luca knew one thing: people could come back.
luca-a-roma-35:s46: He still had to ask for the rest. Not today, but soon.
luca-a-roma-36:s01: Later, when the room was full, Luca looked at the people.
luca-a-roma-36:s02: Speak. Two words. People are here for this place too.
luca-a-roma-36:s03: Me? I don’t know. I am afraid.
luca-a-roma-36:s04: We can handle it, if you want. But it seems to me that you can.
luca-a-roma-36:s05: Luca looked at Nonna Rosa. She smiled and said: “It’s fine like this.”
luca-a-roma-36:s06: Then Luca stopped in the room, near the full tables.
luca-a-roma-36:s07: Good evening. I work here. A few months ago I arrived in Rome, alone.
luca-a-roma-36:s08: Now I have a home, a job, and friends. This café is a part of all this.
luca-a-roma-36:s09: If you like it, come back. Not only today. Also Monday, also Thursday.
luca-a-roma-36:s10: We need people on the days of the week. Not only for a celebration.
luca-a-roma-36:s11: Some people smiled. Some people said “good” quietly.
luca-a-roma-36:s12: The owner listened near the kitchen, without speaking.
luca-a-roma-36:s13: Marco brought a coffee to Nonna Rosa, and she listened to Luca well.
luca-a-roma-36:s14: After the words, the celebration continued. The music was not too loud. People stayed.
luca-a-roma-36:s15: You said little, and you said a lot. All right.
luca-a-roma-36:s16: The owner listened to you. I saw it.
luca-a-roma-36:s17: All right. I only wanted to say one true thing.
luca-a-roma-36:s18: A family asked about the week’s hours. Giulia explained, glad to do more.
luca-a-roma-36:s19: Sofia was near Luca, not like a person who helps a new guy, but like a friend.
luca-a-roma-36:s20: You asked for the right thing. Coming back, not only staying here one day.
luca-a-roma-36:s21: Yes. If they come back, the owner sees work. If not, a nice day remains.
luca-a-roma-36:s22: When the light changed, some people left, and some people stayed longer.
luca-a-roma-36:s23: The owner called Luca near the kitchen, in a not-loud voice.
luca-a-roma-36:s24: Today the café worked. I saw the tables. I saw the people.
luca-a-roma-36:s25: I still don’t know everything. But today yes. You asked well.
luca-a-roma-36:s26: Thank you for saying yes to this celebration.
luca-a-roma-36:s27: You did the work. I only opened the kitchen.
luca-a-roma-36:s28: Luca listened. The owner was talking about today, not about Monday.
luca-a-roma-36:s30: Her too. Tomorrow we talk about hours and work. Not now.
luca-a-roma-36:s31: Giulia heard and made a small sign to Luca: later.
luca-a-roma-36:s32: Sofia told Luca to drink water and to stay still a moment.
luca-a-roma-36:s33: You spoke clearly. Now let’s let the room work.
luca-a-roma-36:s34: Marco washed the plates and said little, as always.
luca-a-roma-36:s35: People stay. This helps more than many words.
luca-a-roma-36:s37: Nonna Rosa paid for the coffee and said she would come back Thursday, if she could.
luca-a-roma-36:s38: The owner heard that and looked at the bill again.
luca-a-roma-36:s39: Come back. We work. We see the week.
luca-a-roma-36:s40: Sofia smiled, truly, not like a person who explains everything.
luca-a-roma-36:s41: When the celebration was almost over, the owner turned the music down a little.
luca-a-roma-36:s42: Today is enough. Tomorrow is Monday. We work.
luca-a-roma-36:s43: Luca helped put the plates in the kitchen and thought about Giulia’s hours.
luca-a-roma-36:s44: The owner had said yes for today. The rest could wait.
luca-a-roma-36:s45: Tomorrow we hear the owner. Today we did enough.
luca-a-roma-36:s46: Yes. Today people arrived. Tomorrow we ask for the rest.
luca-a-roma-36:s47: Sofia looked at the still-full room and spoke quietly.
luca-a-roma-37:s01: Monday morning Luca went to work with a little fear.
luca-a-roma-37:s02: A celebration is one day. Monday is the life of every week.
luca-a-roma-37:s03: When he opened the door, there were already two customers at a table.
luca-a-roma-37:s04: It was not a full room, but it was not empty like the week before.
luca-a-roma-37:s05: Good morning. See? Someone came back.
luca-a-roma-37:s06: Yes. It seems to me a first real day, even if small.
luca-a-roma-37:s07: They worked. The coffee, the water, the bills. Everyday things, but different.
luca-a-roma-37:s08: In the afternoon the owner asked Luca and Giulia to stay a moment.
luca-a-roma-37:s09: I’m not selling. Not now. The café stays. At least this month, and the next.
luca-a-roma-37:s10: Thank you. For me it is important to stay.
luca-a-roma-37:s11: You two work more, if you want. On Saturday I saw that more work is needed. I need hours, not a new person.
luca-a-roma-37:s12: Luca heard the words “if you want” and understood that he could choose.
luca-a-roma-37:s13: Yes. I accept. I need the pay, and I like this place.
luca-a-roma-37:s14: I accept too. But I also want to organize, not only serve.
luca-a-roma-37:s15: All right. We’ll see. You make a weekly plan. I listen.
luca-a-roma-37:s16: Giulia smiled, at last, like a person who was heard.
luca-a-roma-37:s17: For Luca it was good news: the job was staying, and Giulia had real hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s18: A month is not everything. But it was a real start.
luca-a-roma-37:s19: But today they could work without that fear from yesterday.
luca-a-roma-37:s21: A few more hours each week. On Saturday we saw one thing: there is demand. Then we watch the customers.
luca-a-roma-37:s22: If people stay, I give more hours. If not, we change.
luca-a-roma-37:s23: Clear. It is not forever. It is for now.
luca-a-roma-37:s25: In the evening Luca counted the money. This month’s rent was safer.
luca-a-roma-37:s26: He wrote a message to Sofia and Marco: the café stays, for now.
luca-a-roma-37:s27: Sofia answered right away. Marco answered later: on Saturday he saw many people, and he is still looking for work.
luca-a-roma-37:s28: Luca closed the window and thought about the new hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s29: More hours meant more money, and also less free time.
luca-a-roma-37:s30: He had to talk about this with Sofia. It was not something to decide alone.
luca-a-roma-37:s31: Giulia called Luca before leaving and talked about the weekly plan.
luca-a-roma-37:s32: I prepare a clear schedule. You watch the door and the customers.
luca-a-roma-37:s33: All right. And if customers don’t come back?
luca-a-roma-37:s34: Then the owner changes again. But today we have real hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s37: But for the first time after so many weeks, Luca could pay and stay.
luca-a-roma-37:s38: He thought of Marco, still looking for work, and of Sofia, with her full days.
luca-a-roma-37:s39: Tomorrow, or later, he had to see Sofia. He wanted to talk about the new hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s41: When Luca went home, he thought again of Saturday and the full tables.
luca-a-roma-37:s42: That day had given the owner a reason not to sell the café.
luca-a-roma-37:s43: He put the phone near the window and read Sofia’s message again.
luca-a-roma-37:s44: Good. Let’s talk soon about the hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s45: Yes. I accept more, but I don’t want to be left without time for friends.
luca-a-roma-37:s47: The café was staying. Now there were more hours. Luca still had to choose the hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s48: For this evening, that was enough.
luca-a-roma-34:s03:extended: When he opened the door, Giulia was already in the room, with the tables open and ready.
luca-a-roma-34:s18:extended: They put out the plates, the water, and the coffee near the tables. Luca washed the tables twice.
luca-a-roma-35:s04:extended: Wait a moment. It is early. Neighborhood people eat and then go out.
luca-a-roma-35:s20:extended: A woman said she liked the coffee, and that she would come back the next week, for sure.
luca-a-roma-36:s09:extended: If you like it, come back here. Not only today. Also Monday, also Thursday.
luca-a-roma-36:s24:extended: Today the café worked well. I saw the tables. I saw the people.
luca-a-roma-37:s12:extended: Luca heard the words "if you want" and understood that he could choose the hours.
luca-a-roma-37:s14:extended: I accept too. But I also want to organize the week, not only serve.
luca-a-roma-38:s01: Two evenings later, Luca and Sofia met for a dinner in the center.
luca-a-roma-38:s02: The place was small and quiet, with little light and few tables.
luca-a-roma-38:s03: Sofia arrived a little late, because work had been long.
luca-a-roma-38:s04: So. The café is staying. Are you happy about the new hours?
luca-a-roma-38:s05: Yes. I have more money. This month’s rent is safer.
luca-a-roma-38:s06: But I also have less time. The week is already full.
luca-a-roma-38:s07: Luca took the water. Sofia listened, and she did not decide for him.
luca-a-roma-38:s08: What do you want, really? Not what the owner said.
luca-a-roma-38:s09: I want to stay in Rome. I want to work. But I don’t want only work.
luca-a-roma-38:s10: I want time for friends and for home.
luca-a-roma-38:s11: That is clear. Then the hours must not take the whole week.
luca-a-roma-38:s12: While they talked, the room was quiet.
luca-a-roma-38:s13: They ate pasta and talked about Sofia’s work.
luca-a-roma-38:s14: My work is a lot. Some evenings I am tired. Some evenings I am fine.
luca-a-roma-38:s15: Me too. After Saturday, the new hours feel big.
luca-a-roma-38:s16: If you accept all the hours, when do you see your friends?
luca-a-roma-38:s17: I don’t know. Maybe I see friends little. And I don’t like that.
luca-a-roma-38:s18: So it’s not a yes or a no. It’s a question of schedule.
luca-a-roma-38:s19: Luca thought about the rent, then about friends, then about Giulia.
luca-a-roma-38:s20: Giulia makes the week’s plan. I can ask for a clear schedule.
luca-a-roma-38:s21: Yes. Talk to the owner about what you need. He listens.
luca-a-roma-38:s22: When Sofia said “what you need,” Luca understood the important thing.
luca-a-roma-38:s23: He didn’t have to be afraid to ask. He only had to be clear.
luca-a-roma-38:s24: You want more hours, but not all of them. That’s fine.
luca-a-roma-38:s25: They talked about this week, not about a long year.
luca-a-roma-38:s26: Monday and Wednesday evenings, I want to stay free.
luca-a-roma-38:s27: Tuesday and Thursday I can work more, if the owner wants.
luca-a-roma-38:s28: Saturday and Sunday are hard, because the café needs people.
luca-a-roma-38:s29: That seems like a plan to me. It isn’t big, but it’s a start.
luca-a-roma-38:s30: Sofia didn’t say many words. She asked questions, and she listened.
luca-a-roma-38:s31: For me you are a friend, not only the person from the first days.
luca-a-roma-38:s32: I know. Now we talk because we want to, not because you are new.
luca-a-roma-38:s33: Luca smiled. The dinner was small. Every word was clear.
luca-a-roma-38:s34: Tomorrow I talk with the owner. I ask for more hours, but not all.
luca-a-roma-38:s35: Good. And if the owner says no to the hours?
luca-a-roma-38:s36: Then I look for another way. But first I ask.
luca-a-roma-38:s37: After dinner they walked a little toward the neighborhood.
luca-a-roma-38:s38: Rome in the evening was full of people, and they talked quietly.
luca-a-roma-38:s39: They did not decide everything. They decided what to do the next day.
luca-a-roma-38:s40: See you soon. Don’t stay only among the café hours.
luca-a-roma-38:s41: I won’t stay only that way. Monday and Wednesday evenings are free.
luca-a-roma-38:s42: Sofia made a yes sign, happy in a quiet way.
luca-a-roma-38:s43: When Luca got home, he wrote two words on the phone.
luca-a-roma-38:s44: Tomorrow: a clear schedule with the owner. More hours, not all.
luca-a-roma-38:s45: He put the phone near the window and waited a moment.
luca-a-roma-38:s46: The café was staying. The new hours were staying. Now there was also a plan.
luca-a-roma-38:s47: It was a small, clear thing for the new week.
luca-a-roma-38:s49: He thought about Marco, still looking for work, and about Giulia with her plan.
luca-a-roma-38:s50: Then he turned off the light. Tomorrow started with a clear question.
luca-a-roma-38:s09:extended: I want to stay in Rome and I want to work. But I don’t want only work every day.
luca-a-roma-38:s26:extended: Monday and Wednesday evenings, I want to stay free for friends.
luca-a-roma-39:s01: The next day Luca talked with the owner, as decided with Sofia.
luca-a-roma-39:s02: I want more hours, but not all. Monday and Wednesday evenings I want free time.
luca-a-roma-39:s03: Tuesday and Thursday I can do more. Saturday and Sunday, as needed.
luca-a-roma-39:s04: Okay. You’re clear. Let’s make a fair schedule with Giulia.
luca-a-roma-39:s05: Giulia listened from the door and took paper for the plan.
luca-a-roma-39:s06: Good. That way I know who is in the room, and when. I don’t change every day.
luca-a-roma-39:s07: While they were making the schedule, Marco arrived at the café door.
luca-a-roma-39:s08: Sorry. Can I talk a moment? I need to tell you something.
luca-a-roma-39:s09: The owner motioned yes. Luca put the plates on the table.
luca-a-roma-39:s10: I’m looking for work. I haven’t found a job. But on Saturday I saw that help is needed. I can help here.
luca-a-roma-39:s11: On busy days. Few hours. I’m not asking for a job forever.
luca-a-roma-39:s12: Luca looked at Giulia. She looked at the owner, then she spoke.
luca-a-roma-39:s13: On busy days we need one more person. We saw that on Saturday.
luca-a-roma-39:s14: A few hours. Little money. It isn’t a big job. If you want, we’ll try.
luca-a-roma-39:s15: I want to. Thanks. For me it’s already a start.
luca-a-roma-39:s16: Marco motioned yes, and nothing more.
luca-a-roma-39:s17: If you work here, we see each other more. That’s fine for me.
luca-a-roma-39:s18: For me too. Friends and a bit of money. Better than nothing.
luca-a-roma-39:s19: Luca was happy in a quiet way. Marco’s problem remained.
luca-a-roma-39:s20: But there was a real first day at the café, with the people of the place.
luca-a-roma-39:s21: In the afternoon Sofia stopped by, because she wanted to hear the news.
luca-a-roma-39:s22: Marco helps on busy days. It isn’t much, but it’s a place.
luca-a-roma-39:s23: Good. You’re not only looking alone anymore. You have something real.
luca-a-roma-39:s24: Marco said little. Yes. Thanks. Then he looked at Giulia’s schedule.
luca-a-roma-39:s25: Giulia showed the days: a full Saturday, and some evenings in the week.
luca-a-roma-39:s26: You come when the room is full. I organize. Luca has his hours.
luca-a-roma-39:s27: Clear. I do what is needed, and nothing more.
luca-a-roma-39:s29: We’ll try two weeks. Then we look at the customers and the money.
luca-a-roma-39:s30: Nobody said the café was safe forever. But today it was working better.
luca-a-roma-39:s31: Luca saw the new hours on his schedule: more work, but not everything.
luca-a-roma-39:s32: Monday and Wednesday evenings stayed free, as he had told Sofia.
luca-a-roma-39:s33: Sofia stayed a little, because she wanted to be there.
luca-a-roma-39:s34: I’m here because I want to be. Not only because Luca has a problem.
luca-a-roma-39:s35: I know. And I like that.
luca-a-roma-39:s36: Marco took a little water and asked about Saturday’s schedule.
luca-a-roma-39:s37: In the evening the four of them ate near the café, with bread and something to drink.
luca-a-roma-39:s38: It was a dinner after a long day.
luca-a-roma-39:s39: The café is staying. Marco helps. Luca has a clear schedule. I organize.
luca-a-roma-39:s40: I’m here too because I choose to be.
luca-a-roma-39:s42: To Rome, then. And to this small job.
luca-a-roma-39:s43: Luca listened. The group was doing better, but nothing was finished.
luca-a-roma-39:s44: When he got home, he saw a message from his mother on the phone.
luca-a-roma-39:s45: I’ll call you tomorrow. I have a job proposal. It isn’t in Rome.
luca-a-roma-39:s46: Luca read the words twice. He didn’t answer right away.
luca-a-roma-39:s47: He put the phone on the table and looked at Giulia’s schedule, already ready.
luca-a-roma-39:s48: Tomorrow there was the call. Today there was a place for Marco.
luca-a-roma-39:s50: Before sleeping he wrote to Sofia: Tomorrow Mom talks. I’ll tell you after.
luca-a-roma-39:s51: Then he turned off the light. The café was staying. Tomorrow there was the call.

luca-a-roma-40:s39: Luca was staying with the group. Work at the café continued.
luca-a-roma-40:s46: Giulia looked at the tables and spoke quietly.
luca-a-roma-30:s32: They still did not have people for Saturday.
luca-a-roma-30:s33: The difficult news now had a plan, even if small.
luca-a-roma-31:s40: The plan helps. It does not close the problem.

luca-a-roma-25:s34b: He put the money on the table and counted again.
luca-a-roma-25:s34c: Then he thought about the neighborhood café and today’s customers.
luca-a-roma-25:s39: He turned off the light and waited for the next day.

luca-a-roma-26:s33b: Luca closed the door for a moment and looked at the street.

luca-a-roma-27:s32b: They walked a little more and looked at the square.
luca-a-roma-27:s38b: He wrote two words on the phone and read the message again.
luca-a-roma-28:s30b: Luca prepared another coffee and worked near the door.
luca-a-roma-29:s18b: Luca listened to the idea and looked at Sofia.
luca-a-roma-32:s24b: Luca thought about the rent and about Giulia’s hours.
luca-a-roma-32:s24c: Giulia accepted, but for her it was important.

luca-a-roma-41:s01: The first days of October had brought crisp, clean air to the streets of Rome.
luca-a-roma-41:s02: At a quarter past six in the morning, Via Merulana was still almost deserted, illuminated by yellow streetlamps.
luca-a-roma-41:s03: Luca walked briskly with his hands in the pockets of his light jacket.
luca-a-roma-41:s04: He no longer needed an alarm clock; his body now knew the natural rhythm of the city.
luca-a-roma-41:s05: In front of the café, he opened the heavy padlock and lifted the metal shutter with a confident motion.
luca-a-roma-41:s06: A year earlier, that metallic clatter gave him a subtle feeling of anxiety.
luca-a-roma-41:s07: Today, instead, it simply meant that the workday was beginning.
luca-a-roma-41:s08: He walked into the bar, turned on the lights, and started up the large coffee machine.
luca-a-roma-41:s09: While the boiler built up pressure, he prepared the cups and pitchers of fresh milk on the marble counter.
luca-a-roma-41:s10: At a quarter to seven, the bakery van arrived with warm croissants.
luca-a-roma-41:s11: Luca signed the delivery slip on the counter with ease.
luca-a-roma-41:s12: Shortly after, Giulia walked in with her usual straightforward energy.
luca-a-roma-41:s13: "Good morning, Luca. Is the machine already ready?"
luca-a-roma-41:s14: "Completely ready. The steam is at full pressure and the croissants just arrived."
luca-a-roma-41:s15: Between seven and eight-thirty, the café filled up with neighborhood customers.
luca-a-roma-41:s16: Luca and Giulia worked side by side in perfect harmony.
luca-a-roma-41:s17: While Giulia rang up receipts at the cash register, Luca pulled espressos and steamed milk without making a single mistake.
luca-a-roma-41:s18: He knew by heart that Signor Moretti wanted a short espresso in a glass with half a packet of sugar.
luca-a-roma-41:s19: In those moments, Luca felt a deep satisfaction: he was no longer a disoriented small-town boy, but a recognized presence in Rome.
luca-a-roma-41:s20: Usually, the owner Bruno arrived around half past seven.
luca-a-roma-41:s21: He would enter with the newspaper, greet everyone loudly, and have a macchiato before taking his place at the register.
luca-a-roma-41:s22: But on that Wednesday, the clock hands reached eight-thirty without any sign of Bruno.
luca-a-roma-41:s23: At a quarter to nine, the glass door opened slowly.
luca-a-roma-41:s24: Bruno walked in with a heavy step, holding a thick dark binder of documents under his arm.
luca-a-roma-41:s25: He did not greet the customers at the counter and did not take off his coat.
luca-a-roma-41:s26: He went straight to the small table at the back of the room and sat down with a sigh, rubbing his leg.
luca-a-roma-41:s27: Giulia stepped up to Luca behind the coffee machine and spoke in a low voice.
luca-a-roma-41:s28: "Did you see Bruno? It seems that something is strange this morning."
luca-a-roma-41:s29: "Yes, I noticed right away. I don't think he is feeling very well physically, or he has some serious worries."
luca-a-roma-41:s30: "I think the accounts with the accountant are heavier than expected. Look at that folder: he was at Dr. Marini's office until late yesterday evening."
luca-a-roma-41:s31: Luca prepared a small cup of hot macchiato and brought it to the table at the back of the room.
luca-a-roma-41:s32: On the table were sheets covered in numbers and balance sheet tables.
luca-a-roma-41:s34: Bruno looked up from the papers with a tired but affectionate glance.
luca-a-roma-41:s35: "Thank you, Luca. It's important that the place runs well even when I arrive late."
luca-a-roma-41:s36: He took a sip, looking for a moment at the room full of voices.
luca-a-roma-41:s37: "Thirty-five years, Luca. Sometimes it seems that time flies by in a breath, and sometimes it seems to weigh like a boulder."
luca-a-roma-41:s38: Luca hesitated for a moment; he feared that any word might seem out of place.
luca-a-roma-41:s39: "It's normal that after so many years there are harder days, Signor Bruno. If you need me to work a few extra hours, just let me know."
luca-a-roma-41:s40: Bruno gave him a gentle pat on the arm.
luca-a-roma-41:s41: "You're a good young man. Go on back to the counter with Giulia. I need to finish reading these papers before eleven."
luca-a-roma-41:s42: Around a quarter past eleven, before the lunch service began, Bruno stood up.
luca-a-roma-41:s43: He closed the black folder and placed the spare cash register key in front of Luca.
luca-a-roma-41:s44: "I have an appointment outside the neighborhood and won't be back for lunch. You two close at three for the break. See you tomorrow at seven."
luca-a-roma-41:s45: Bruno walked out onto the sidewalk of Via Merulana, walking slowly toward the tram stop.
luca-a-roma-41:s46: It was the first time in over a year that Bruno left the café before lunch.
luca-a-roma-41:s47: Luca picked up the metal key and put it into his apron pocket.
luca-a-roma-41:s48: From the kitchen came the aroma of fresh pasta sauce, and the first midday customers walked in.
luca-a-roma-41:s49: Everything was functioning with its usual precision, but Luca felt that something invisible had just begun to change.
luca-a-roma-42:s01: On Thursday evenings the bar closed at eight o'clock sharp.
luca-a-roma-42:s02: Giulia had finished her shift, cleaned the coffee machine, and left toward the metro.
luca-a-roma-42:s03: Luca had lowered the shutter halfway, letting in only the fresh evening air.
luca-a-roma-42:s04: While sweeping the marble floor, he noticed that Bruno was still sitting at the table at the back of the room.
luca-a-roma-42:s05: Under the warm light of a hanging lamp, the old owner had opened two large cardboard boxes and a dozen colored folders.
luca-a-roma-42:s06: "Luca, do you have five minutes before going home?" Bruno asked in a calm voice, without looking up from the papers.
luca-a-roma-42:s07: "Of course, Signor Bruno. I've almost finished tidying the counter. Do you need help with those papers?"
luca-a-roma-42:s08: "Yes. Sit down here with me. It's important that you see how the numbers of this place really work."
luca-a-roma-42:s09: Luca leaned the broom in the corner, took off his apron, and sat down across from Bruno.
luca-a-roma-42:s10: On the table were supplier invoices divided by category: fresh milk, coffee roasting, bakery goods, and beverages.
luca-a-roma-42:s11: Next to them was a handwritten list with all the payment deadlines for October.
luca-a-roma-42:s12: Bruno handed him a red folder with the accounts from the past six months.
luca-a-roma-42:s13: "Take this calculator, Luca. Add up the items for electricity and gas."
luca-a-roma-42:s14: Luca typed the numbers one by one into the gray display.
luca-a-roma-42:s15: When he saw the total, he was surprised: the utility bills had doubled compared to the year before.
luca-a-roma-42:s16: "Customers see the bar full every morning and think we make a fortune," Bruno said with a wry half-smile.
luca-a-roma-42:s17: "But if the cost of raw coffee and electricity rises every month and we keep the espresso price at one euro twenty, the profit margin disappears almost entirely."
luca-a-roma-42:s18: For the first time, Luca understood the fundamental difference between total revenue and the actual net profit left at the end of the month.
luca-a-roma-42:s19: Bruno took a balance sheet stamped by the accountant and slid it across the table.
luca-a-roma-42:s20: "I fear that the fixed costs have become too heavy for a single person."
luca-a-roma-42:s21: "There is the rent of the premises to pay every month, municipal waste taxes, and the installments on the old kitchen loan."
luca-a-roma-42:s22: "Can't the price of coffee be raised by thirty cents to offset costs?" Luca asked cautiously.
luca-a-roma-42:s23: "I doubt neighborhood residents would accept such a steep increase without complaining or going to the café in the next square."
luca-a-roma-42:s24: "In Rome, coffee isn't just a drink; it's a social ritual. If you touch that price, you touch a delicate balance."
luca-a-roma-42:s25: "A venue needs to find new revenue, perhaps through evening aperitifs or higher-end food service, but doing that requires investment and fresh energy."
luca-a-roma-42:s26: Bruno set his pen down on the notebook and leaned back against the wooden chair, massaging his leg with both hands.
luca-a-roma-42:s27: His eyes revealed a deep exhaustion that didn't come merely from that single day's hours of work.
luca-a-roma-42:s28: "Tell me something, Luca. How old is your father?"
luca-a-roma-42:s29: "He turns sixty in November," Luca replied, surprised by the personal question.
luca-a-roma-42:s30: "He still works in the fields in Pietralba, but in the evenings he sits down early by the fireplace because his back aches."
luca-a-roma-42:s31: Bruno nodded slowly, his gaze fixed on the empty mirrors of the bar.
luca-a-roma-42:s32: "Right. Your father understands exactly what I mean. At a certain age, the body starts demanding payment for every past exertion."
luca-a-roma-42:s33: "It's not that I lack passion; it's that every morning I feel the weight of thirty-five years of dawn wake-ups."
luca-a-roma-42:s34: Luca listened in silence, feeling a tightness in his chest: he understood that Bruno was not just talking about bills and suppliers, but sharing the limits of his physical stamina.
luca-a-roma-42:s35: He feared that any attempt to reassure him might seem naive in front of such an evident reality.
luca-a-roma-42:s36: Around a quarter past nine, they put the folders back into the cardboard boxes.
luca-a-roma-42:s37: Bruno locked the office drawer and switched off the lamp above the table.
luca-a-roma-42:s38: "Thank you for the help with the invoices, Luca. It's important that you know these aspects of the business."
luca-a-roma-42:s39: "Behind a good coffee at the counter there is always a complex machine that requires constant care and attention."
luca-a-roma-42:s40: "Thank you for your trust, Signor Bruno. I learned a lot this evening."
luca-a-roma-42:s41: They went out together onto the deserted sidewalk of Via Merulana and lowered the metal shutter completely.
luca-a-roma-42:s42: Bruno said goodbye to Luca with a warm handshake and headed toward the tram stop, while Luca started walking toward San Lorenzo.
luca-a-roma-42:s43: As he walked beneath the streetlamps, Luca felt that his view of the future was becoming more serious with every step.
luca-a-roma-43:s01: On Saturday afternoon, lunch service had finished around half past two, leaving the warm aroma of coffee in the room.
luca-a-roma-43:s02: The last table of regular customers had paid their bill at the register and stepped out into the golden October light.
luca-a-roma-43:s03: From the kitchen, the cook Salvatore turned off the burners, put away his knives, and said goodbye to everyone before heading home for the weekend.
luca-a-roma-43:s04: Bruno turned the key in the lock of the glass door, flipped the sign to "Closed," and gave a calm nod to Luca and Giulia.
luca-a-roma-43:s05: "Leave the dishes for a few minutes and come sit down at table four near the window," the owner said in a quiet voice.
luca-a-roma-43:s06: He placed a pitcher of fresh water and three clear glass tumblers on the marble table.
luca-a-roma-43:s07: Giulia and Luca exchanged a quick knowing look, surprised by such a formal request right before the afternoon break.
luca-a-roma-43:s08: They sat down next to each other on the dark wooden chairs, waiting in silence for Bruno to begin speaking.
luca-a-roma-43:s09: Bruno poured the water into the three glasses without rushing, looking them in the eyes with great frankness and affection.
luca-a-roma-43:s10: "I called you here because I want you to hear the truth directly from me, before uncontrolled rumors start circulating in the neighborhood."
luca-a-roma-43:s11: "I have spoken at length with the accountant and with my family: I have officially decided to transfer the license and the business by the end of May."
luca-a-roma-43:s12: "The doctor confirmed that my knee needs rest, and my daughter in Bologna has her own career and has no intention of running the place."
luca-a-roma-43:s13: "I want you to be informed in advance, so that you have all the necessary time to reflect and get organized."
luca-a-roma-43:s14: Bruno's words echoed clear, weighty, and definitive in the quiet dining room.
luca-a-roma-43:s15: Giulia was the first to react, displaying her customary practical and professional promptness.
luca-a-roma-43:s16: She had worked in the bars and restaurants of central Rome for many years and knew well how commercial sales operated.
luca-a-roma-43:s17: "I completely understand your decision, Signor Bruno, and it is right that you think of your health and retirement," she said in a respectful but direct tone.
luca-a-roma-43:s18: "I would like to understand what will happen with our employment contracts: will whoever buys the business keep the current staff, or should we start looking for a new job right away?"
luca-a-roma-43:s19: "It depends on who takes over the management of the venue," Bruno replied with utmost honesty.
luca-a-roma-43:s20: "But I guarantee that you will receive every euro of your severance pay and severance fund right down to the last working day."
luca-a-roma-43:s21: "Furthermore, I will write for both of you excellent letters of recommendation for any employer in Rome."
luca-a-roma-43:s22: "I only ask that you continue working with me with your usual diligence and care until the definitive closing of the spring season."
luca-a-roma-43:s23: "No problem on my part, Signor Bruno. I know several dining room managers near Piazza Barberini and I'll start looking around quietly after the Christmas holidays," Giulia answered, already looking ahead with lucidity to the next steps.
luca-a-roma-43:s24: Luca, on the other hand, remained completely still, unable to utter a single word.
luca-a-roma-43:s25: He stared at the polished marble surface of the table, feeling a sudden, deep hollowness in his stomach.
luca-a-roma-43:s26: For Giulia, that bar was a serious and respectable job, but easily replaceable with another counter in another Roman neighborhood.
luca-a-roma-43:s27: For Luca, however, this place represented the entire foundation and heart of his life in Rome.
luca-a-roma-43:s28: It was here that he had arrived from Termini station with a single suitcase; here Bruno had put his trust in him; here he had met Sofia, Giulia, and his neighborhood friends.
luca-a-roma-43:s29: He suddenly realized that selling the business didn't just mean a change in commercial management, but called into question his very stay in the capital.
luca-a-roma-43:s30: "What do you think, Luca? You seem very quiet," Bruno asked with a gentle, fatherly voice.
luca-a-roma-43:s31: "Thank you for your honesty, Signor Bruno. I just need to process this news. I will do my best every day until May, I promise you with all my heart."
luca-a-roma-43:s32: Around half past three they ended the meeting and rinsed the glasses in the stainless steel sink.
luca-a-roma-43:s33: Bruno shook both their hands warmly: "I don't want you to live these months with anxiety or fear. Let's work well together as we always have."
luca-a-roma-43:s34: Giulia grabbed her shoulder bag and walked away briskly, already talking on the phone with a friend in the hospitality sector.
luca-a-roma-43:s35: Luca stepped out onto the sidewalk of Via Merulana under a clear, bright early autumn sky.
luca-a-roma-43:s36: Passersby strolled peacefully gazing into shop windows, unaware that inside the café something fundamental had just broken forever.
luca-a-roma-43:s37: Luca pulled his phone from his pocket and typed a message to Sofia: "Do you have an hour free tonight in Monti? Something very important happened at the café and I'd like to talk to you in person."
luca-a-roma-43:s38: He slipped his phone back into his jacket and set off walking toward San Lorenzo, aware that the countdown for his future in Rome had officially begun.
